title: Nonlinear Route, Choice, Consequence & Dependency Graph
objective: Extend the prepared MAS Adventure workspace with deterministic nonlinear route, choice, consequence and dependency-graph authoring on top of MAS-02 structure and MAS-03 assembly, while preserving explicit references, fail-closed validation and the boundary between prepared authoring semantics and live runtime/state mutation.

scope.purpose: Represent prepared nonlinear routes, choices, consequences and dependencies inside the MAS authoring workspace without executing them as live runtime transitions or duplicating canonical Action/Event/Adventure state authority.
scope.completion_gate: A representative MAS workspace can deterministically express nonlinear routes, choices, consequences and dependencies over prepared MAS structure/assembly with explicit references and fail-closed invalid states, while preserving canonical owner/runtime authority and never treating the prepared graph as executed live truth.

selection_boundaries: Existing MAS validation family remains active; no family transition is authorized or required.
MAS-01 workspace/document authority, MAS-02 higher-order structure and MAS-03 prepared assembly remain foundational and are not reopened silently.
Routes, choices, consequences and dependencies are prepared authoring semantics in MAS-04; execution and canonical mutation remain with CNI, Action/Event and other canonical runtime owners.
Prepared graph reachability or consequences never prove that a transition, choice, encounter or event occurred.
Branching, node-based, sandbox and hybrid authoring are supported without requiring a single golden route.
MAS-05 retains quest/objective/mission/task/milestone authoring scope and must not be pulled forward.
CNI-12 and PCA remain unselected; MAS-05+ and SMB-08 remain unauthorized.
next_action: On the authorized application branch, establish causal MAS-04 RED against deterministic prepared nonlinear route/choice/consequence/dependency graph behavior, then implement the minimum contract without reopening MAS-01..03 authority boundaries.
